chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Inform me about the muḥṣan—if he flees from the pit, is he to be returned so that the hadd may be carried out upon him? He said: “He is returned, and he is not returned.” I said: How is that?

He said: “If he is one who confessed against himself, then fled from the pit after some of the stones had struck him, he is not returned. But if the evidence was established against him while he denied it, then he fled, he is returned in humiliation until the hadd is carried out upon him. That is because Māʿiz ibn Mālik confessed before the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to zina, so he ordered that he be stoned. Then he fled from the pit, and al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām struck him with the leg-bone of a camel and hamstrung him, so he fell, and the people caught up with him and killed him. Then they informed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم of that, and he said: ‘Why did you not leave him, when he fled, to go away? For he was only the one who had confessed against himself.’”

He said: “And he said to them: ‘Indeed, had ʿAlī been present with you, you would not have gone astray.’” He said: “And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم paid his blood-money from the treasury of the Muslims.”

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legal proof or evidentiary testimony establishing the case
key_terms.الْحُفْرَةِ: the pit from which the condemned person fled during stoning
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنِ: a legally protected married person subject to the hadd ruling for zina in this context
key_terms.الْمُقِرَّ: the one who confesses against himself
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.يُرْجَمَ: to be stoned as the hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: If a muḥṣan flees during the hadd punishment of stoning, should he be brought back?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal distinction in the hadd of zina for a muḥṣan who flees during stoning: one who confessed voluntarily is not returned, while one convicted by evidence despite denial is returned until the punishment is completed. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling through the case of Māʿiz ibn Mālik and also highlights the decisive guidance of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in judicial matters.
